chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqi, who said:

I wrote to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) the second: Is it permissible to take out from what is obligatory in the crops, from the wheat and the barley, and what is obligatory upon the gold, dirhams, being the value of what equates to it, or is it not permissible except to take out from each thing that which is in it? So he (peace be upon him) answered: Whichever is easier, take out.
ai.seo_question: Can I pay Zakat on crops or gold in cash instead of the actual goods?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the principle of *al-taysir* (ease) in Zakat payments, allowing the payer to choose between delivering the actual agricultural produce or gold and paying their monetary equivalent. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly view that the primary objective is the fulfillment of the obligation, granting flexibility based on the payer's convenience and local economic conditions. It underscores the pragmatic nature of Ja'fari jurisprudence in adapting religious duties to practical realities.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Khalid al Barqy who sid,

‘I wrote to Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> the 2<sup>nd</sup>, ‘Is it allowed if one were to take out from what is Obligated regarding the farm, from the wheat and the barley, and what is Obligated upon the gold, as Dirhams, being the price of what equates to it, or is it not allowed except to take out from everything whatever it (actually) is?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> answered: ‘Whichever is easier, take out’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqiy who has said the following: “

I once wrote to abu al-Hassan, al-Thaniy, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, and asked him (the Imam) if it is permissible to pay Zakat which is due on grains, like wheat and barley and on gold by means of dirham in equal value or is it necessary to pay from the same substance on which Zakat is due? He (the Imam) answered, ‘Whichever is available can be paid as Zakat.”’
